title: Hallock Site
summary: The Hallock Site is associated with a seventeenth-century stone-working and village landscape. Its precise archaeological deposits are not publicly identified.
ancestral_territory_note: Shown in relation to Corchaug Ancestral Land on the current ancestral territory map.
why_this_matters: The discovery of a seventeenth-century flaking workshop containing three thousand stone scrapers provides remarkable evidence of intense, specialized indigenous tool production. Unearthing such massive concentrations of everyday working implements demonstrates that early Native communities were not merely temporary camps, but highly organized, industrious centers of local manufacturing.

source_list.title: Jeremy Dennis, On This Site
